subject: Budget gateways & procurement triggers — follow-up and ask
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anita Kumar <anita.k@orbitai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Budget gateways & procurement triggers — follow-up and ask

Hi Anita — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap from my side and two asks so we can align internally on pricing/commit strategy: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Target workload: production recommender + nightly embeddings for ~2M API calls / month (average context 512 tokens, peak L7 higher).
- Current experimentation: 150k tokens/day across dev + staging, planning scale after Q3 POC.
- Procurement model at Orbit: centralized PO for >$50k, month-to-month for smaller vendor spend. Finance prefers a committed band for discounts.

Two asks (so we can size proposals):
1) Can you confirm a monthly spend band you’re comfortable committing to for the first 6–12 months? Rough bands are fine (e.g., <$10k, $10–50k, $50–150k, >$150k).
2) What procurement threshold triggers a purchase order and who signs it? (we saw mention of $50k but want the exact cutoff and lead contact)

Our posture and options:
- If you can commit to a 6–12 month reserved band, we can propose a blended unit price and a modest overage discount.
- For smaller initial spend we can offer upfront credits + usage-based pricing to avoid procurement friction.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the preferred band and PO threshold (ask 1–2 lines).
- I’ll build 2 pricing scenarios: (A) low-commit (credits + pay-as-you-go) and (B) reserved band (6 or 12 month) with target $/1M token levels.

I attached a short draft MAP so you can see milestones we typically align on (PO, pilot, rollout).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Lauren from our deals team if we need to escalate procurement flex.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft_MAP_OrbitAI_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Kumar <anita.k@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Budget gateways & procurement triggers — follow-up and ask

Internal note but keeping Anita in the loop — Rishi, good framing. A couple tactical levers if Orbit lands in the $50–150k band:

- Standard reserved band: 12-month commit at a 20% discount vs list baseline; we can tier further for 24 months.
- Overdraft protection: allow 10% temporary overage to avoid outage, bill at standard unit rate and true-up monthly.
- PO flexibility: If procurement needs a signed SOW + PO, Sales Ops can accept a PO net-30 against a signed SOW. If they need vendor onboarding docs, we can surface SOC2 + data retention addendum.

Notes for pricing scenarios: include a target $/1M token metric in each scenario. Rishi — when you get the band from Anita, send me the expected monthly token average and 95th percentile so I can build the blended unit economics.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Anita Kumar <anita.k@orbitai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@orbitai.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget gateways & procurement triggers — follow-up and ask

Hi Rishi — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from procurement/finance: 

- Budget band: for the pilot (Q3) we have an internal allocation that maps to the $10–50k monthly band. If the POC shows 60–80% of target performance we can move to $50–150k/month for full rollout in Q4.
- Formal PO trigger: any vendor annualized spend >$60k requires a PO and centralized review. For monthly billing under that, we can do credit card or monthly invoices.
- Signers: CFO (Priya Menon) signs >$150k commitments; Head of Procurement (Sam Li) approves POs in the $60k–$150k band.

Attached is Orbit AI's procurement checklist — it lists required vendor docs and onboarding steps.

Quick question: what would a target dollar baseline look like for a 12-month reserved band at ~75k/month? Specifically, we want an indicative $/1M token rate to plug into our internal cost model.

Best,
Anita Kumar
Head of Data Platforms | Orbit AI
attachments: Procurement_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anita Kumar <anita.k@orbitai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget gateways & procurement triggers — follow-up and ask

Thanks Anita — this is exactly what we needed. Below I’ll give two indicative scenarios (very high level) to help you with the internal model. I’ll follow with a formal quote once you confirm the band and token distribution.

Assumptions I’m using (please flag if different):
- Avg tokens per API call: 512 (context + response), monthly API calls ~2M -> monthly tokens ~1.024B (~1,024M tokens).
- Peak/99th percentile bumps may push to ~1.3B in busy months — we’ll model headroom in the MAP.

Indicative scenarios (12-month commitment at ~75k/month baseline):
A) Reserved band — 12 months, $75k/mo commitment
  - Blended unit: $650 per 1M tokens (example; includes KV cache savings and batching optimization estimate)
  - Annualized value: $900k
  - Overage: billed at $850/1M tokens beyond 10% buffer, with 30-day true-up

B) Low-commit (credits + PAYG)
  - Effective unit (with $100k upfront credit + PAYG): ~$900 per 1M tokens until credits exhausted
  - No PO required for pilot if paying monthly invoice under $60k threshold

Next steps: 
- If Orbit confirms the $50–150k band trigger for rollout and the $60k PO cutoff, we’ll draft a formal 12-month SOW and pricing sheet.
- I’ll include the target $/1M token lines for reserved vs PAYG in the quote; Lauren will help finalize discounting.

Can we lock a 15-minute sync early next week (Mon/Tue) for me, Lauren, and Sam Li (procurement) to run through the onboarding checklist? If so, please propose a time or I can send a calendar invite.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
